question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher requirement for a vessel less than 26 feet long, without a fixed fire-extinguishing system, that meets one of the conditions triggering the requirement?
choice_a: No extinguisher is required regardless of conditions
choice_c: A fixed system is mandatory at that length
explanation: A vessel less than 26 feet long without a fixed fire-extinguishing system must carry one B-I (5-B rated) portable extinguisher if it meets a triggering condition, such as having an inboard engine or closed fuel storage.
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Number and Type of Required Fire Extinguishers

question: How many fire extinguishers must a vessel 40 feet to less than 65 feet long carry if it has no fixed fire-extinguishing system?
choice_a: Three B-I (5-B) extinguishers, or one B-II (20-B) and one B-I (5-B)
choice_c: No extinguisher is needed at that length
explanation: Without a fixed fire-extinguishing system, a vessel 40 feet to less than 65 feet long must carry three B-I (5-B) extinguishers, or one B-II (20-B) plus one B-I (5-B).
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Number and Type of Required Fire Extinguishers

question: If a vessel 40 feet to less than 65 feet long has an approved fixed fire-extinguishing system installed, how many additional portable extinguishers must it also carry?
choice_a: None -- the fixed system alone satisfies the requirement
choice_b: Two B-I (5-B) extinguishers, or one B-II (20-B) extinguisher
explanation: A vessel 40 to less than 65 feet long with an approved fixed system installed must still carry two B-I (5-B) portable extinguishers, or one B-II (20-B), in addition to the fixed system.
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Number and Type of Required Fire Extinguishers

question: With an approved fixed fire-extinguishing system installed, how many additional portable fire extinguishers must a vessel less than 26 feet long carry?
explanation: For vessels less than 26 feet long, an approved fixed fire-extinguishing system fully satisfies the requirement, so no additional portable extinguisher is required.
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Number and Type of Required Fire Extinguishers

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the conditions used to judge whether a fire extinguisher is in good and serviceable condition?
choice_a: It is charged and shows a charged reading on its gauge or indicator, if equipped
choice_b: Its pin lock is firmly in place
choice_c: Its discharge nozzle is clean and free of obstructions
choice_d: It is painted a bright, visible color
explanation: Serviceability depends on being charged, having the pin lock firmly in place, showing no significant corrosion or damage, and having a clean, unobstructed nozzle -- paint color is not one of the recognized conditions.
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Keeping Fire Extinguishers Readily Accessible and in Good and Serviceable Condition

question: What must be true about a fire extinguisher's age and history for it to be considered serviceable?
choice_a: It must not be expired or appear to have been previously used
choice_b: It only needs to be less than 20 years old
choice_c: Expired extinguishers are acceptable if kept in a locker
choice_d: There is no expiration standard for boat fire extinguishers
explanation: A serviceable fire extinguisher must not be expired and must not appear to have been previously discharged or used.
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Keeping Fire Extinguishers Readily Accessible and in Good and Serviceable Condition

question: Which vessels are prohibited from being equipped with a siren as a sound-producing device?
choice_b: All vessels except those used by law enforcement officers
choice_d: There is no restriction on sirens
explanation: No vessel may be equipped with a siren except vessels used by law enforcement officers.
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Requirements to Have Sound-Producing Devices

question: Can a person's own voice satisfy a vessel's requirement to carry a sound-producing device?
choice_a: Yes, shouting is always an acceptable substitute
choice_c: No -- an efficient sound-producing device such as a whistle, horn, or similar mechanical device is required; a human voice is not acceptable
choice_d: Only if the operator has completed a boater safety course
explanation: Vessels less than 39.4 feet (12 meters), including PWC, must have a means of making an efficient sound signal, such as a handheld air horn, athletic whistle, or installed horn; a human voice does not satisfy the requirement.
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Requirements to Have Sound-Producing Devices

question: In a gasoline vessel's ventilation system, where must the intake duct terminate?
choice_a: Outside the hull, pointed away from the vessel
choice_b: Directly above the exhaust duct opening
choice_c: There is no requirement for where the intake duct terminates
choice_d: At a point at least midway to the bilge, or below the level of the carburetor air intake
explanation: The ventilation system requires at least two ducts fitted with cowls: an exhaust duct extending from the open atmosphere to the lower bilge, and an intake duct extending to at least midway to the bilge or below the carburetor air intake level.

question: How should a vessel with a natural (non-powered) ventilation system, such as a PWC, be checked for gasoline vapors before starting the engine?
choice_a: Open the engine compartment and check for the smell of gasoline fumes
choice_b: Run the engine briefly to see if it stalls
choice_c: No check is necessary if the system is natural rather than powered
choice_d: Spray water into the compartment and check for bubbles
explanation: Vessels with natural (non-powered) ventilation, such as most PWC, should have the operator open the engine compartment and check by smell for gasoline vapors before starting the engine.

question: What warning must be posted near the instrument panel of a gasoline-powered vessel built after July 31, 1980, that has a power ventilation blower in the engine compartment?
choice_a: A sticker listing the vessel's registration number
choice_b: A sticker warning that gasoline vapors can explode and instructing the operator to run the blower four minutes and check by smell for vapors before starting
choice_c: No warning sticker is required regardless of build date
choice_d: A sticker warning about carbon monoxide only
explanation: Vessels built after July 31, 1980 with a power exhaust blower in a gasoline engine compartment must display a warning sticker near the instrument panel stating that gasoline vapors can explode and instructing the operator to run the blower four minutes and check by smell before starting the engine.

question: Which recreational vessels are exempt from carrying day-use visual distress signals on Washington's coastal waters (though night signals are still required if operating between sunset and sunrise)?
choice_b: Only vessels with an inboard engine
choice_c: Recreational vessels under 16 feet, non-motorized open sailboats under 26 feet, and manually propelled vessels
choice_d: No vessel is ever exempt from VDS requirements
explanation: Recreational vessels under 16 feet, non-motorized open sailboats under 26 feet, and manually propelled vessels are exempt from carrying day signals, but all vessels on coastal waters must still carry night signals when operating between sunset and sunrise.
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Requirements to Carry Visual Distress Signals (VDSs)

question: When is a boater legally permitted to display visual distress signals on the water?
choice_b: Only between the hours of noon and 2 p.m.
choice_c: Only when returning to a marina
choice_d: Only when assistance is required to prevent immediate or potential danger to persons on board a vessel
explanation: It is prohibited to display visual distress signals on the water unless assistance is required to prevent immediate or potential danger to persons on board a vessel.
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Requirements to Carry Visual Distress Signals (VDSs)

question: Which of these is an approved combination of visual distress signals that meets requirements for both day and night use?
choice_d: A boat horn plus an anchor light
explanation: Three handheld red flares is one of the approved combinations that satisfies both day and night visual distress signal requirements; another is one handheld red flare plus two red meteors.
source_note: boat-ed.com/washington, Combinations of VDSs That Meet Requirements

question: What must an electric distress light do to qualify as a night-use visual distress signal?
choice_a: Simply produce a steady white beam
choice_b: Automatically flash the international SOS distress signal
choice_c: Be red in color and mounted at the bow
choice_d: It can be any ordinary flashlight
explanation: An electric distress light qualifies as a night-only visual distress signal only if it automatically flashes the international SOS distress signal.

question: What are the minimum size and markings for an orange distress flag used as a day-only visual distress signal?
choice_a: At least 12 inches square, solid orange with no markings
choice_b: Any size flag as long as it is orange
choice_c: At least 3 feet by 3 feet, showing a black square and ball on an orange background
choice_d: It must be triangular and reflective
explanation: The orange distress flag, a day-only signal, must measure at least 3 feet by 3 feet and display a black square and ball on an orange background.
